identification.summary: Chaya_004 is the name Forescout (Vedere Labs) uses for a likely China-based threat actor, identified from malicious infrastructure: a network of servers hosting SuperShell backdoors, often on Chinese cloud providers, alongside various penetration-testing tools, many of Chinese origin [S1][S2]. Forescout linked the infrastructure to exploitation of SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 (CVSS 10.0), an unauthenticated upload flaw in Visual Composer that allows web shell upload and remote code execution [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Forescout reports exploitation of CVE-2025-31324 observed since at least 2025-04-29 on its Adversary Engagement Environment [S1].
identification.notes: Forescout's Chaya_NNN naming is a vendor-internal tracking label and no Microsoft name or MITRE group is known for it. Several other China-nexus clusters (UNC5221, UNC5174, CL-STA-0048) were reported by EclecticIQ as exploiting the same SAP flaw; those are separate vendor clusters and are not merged with Chaya_004 here [S4].

attribution.confidence: Forescout assesses the actor as likely China-based [S1][S2]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Forescout cites infrastructure on Chinese cloud providers and mostly Chinese-origin tools [S1][S2]. The SuperShell tool is a Go web reverse shell that The Hacker News coverage of Forescout's report ties to a Chinese-speaking developer [S2].

targeting.notes: The sources reviewed do not name Chaya_004 victims, sectors or regions. Separate EclecticIQ reporting on China-nexus actors exploiting the same SAP flaw lists critical-infrastructure sectors, but it does not tie them to Chaya_004 [S3][S4].

capabilities.summary: Exploits CVE-2025-31324 in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer via the /developmentserver/metadatauploader endpoint to upload web shells [S1][S2]. Forescout recovered an ELF binary named config from an attack that pointed to IP 47.97.42.177 hosting a SuperShell login page, and the same infrastructure hosted additional pen-testing tools [S2]. Per coverage of the report, a port on that host presented a self-signed certificate impersonating Cloudflare [S2]. Tools reported on the infrastructure include NPS, SoftEther VPN, Cobalt Strike and Asset Reconnaissance Lighthouse [S2].

campaigns.name: SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 exploitation observed by Forescout
campaigns.summary: Forescout reports exploitation observed since at least this date via scans and attempts on its Adversary Engagement Environment, with infrastructure later linked to Chaya_004 [S1].

campaigns.name: Forescout publishes Chaya_004 infrastructure analysis
campaigns.summary: Forescout's Vedere Labs publishes analysis of SuperShell-hosting infrastructure and TTPs, with mitigation recommendations; The Hacker News covers it [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: Likely China-based actor tracked by Forescout as Chaya_004; sponsor unknown [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: CVE-2025-31324 exploitation, web shell upload, SuperShell reverse shell, and Chinese-origin pen-testing tools [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Servers on Chinese cloud providers, including IP 47.97.42.177 hosting a SuperShell login page [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Internet-exposed SAP NetWeaver AS Java systems with Visual Composer enabled [S1][S2].

gaps: Forescout's original blog could not be fetched in this environment (host unreachable). Details come from search-result excerpts and The Hacker News coverage of the report [S1][S2]; confirm against the primary text.
Victims, sectors, objectives and sponsor are not established in the sources gathered.
Relationship to UNC5221, UNC5174 and CL-STA-0048 (EclecticIQ) and to ransomware actors reported exploiting the same flaw is unknown [S4].
Exploitation start dates differ by source (January, March or 29 April 2025); Chaya_004 specific activity before 2025-04-29 is unverified [S1].
Specific cloud provider names and the full indicator list were not verified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-exposed SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer servers are key terrain; they sit on enterprise networks holding business data [S1]. STEP 2: The actor's infrastructure relies on Chinese cloud hosting and Chinese-origin tooling, which limits what is knowable about intent [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is exploit CVE-2025-31324, upload a web shell, then use SuperShell and pen-testing tooling for access [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is opportunistic exploitation of unpatched SAP servers; MDCOA is use of that foothold for persistent access in defense-industry or logistics enterprise systems (not sourced; no victims confirmed). Candidate indicators: requests to /developmentserver/metadatauploader, unexpected files on NetWeaver servers, outbound connections to 47.97.42.177 and to hosts with SuperShell login pages [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Track SAP Security Note 3594142 patch status on mission-supporting ERP systems for situational awareness [S3]. (2) Mitigations reported by Forescout: apply SAP patches, restrict the metadata uploader endpoint, disable Visual Composer if unneeded, and monitor for unusual service changes [S1]. (3) Several actors exploited the same flaw, so prioritize containment over attribution [S4]. (4) Coordinate with system owners and DIB partners hosting SAP; authorities for remediation rest with the owning organization.

provenance.importedSummary: Chaya_004 is a Chinese threat actor identified through malicious infrastructure, including a network of servers hosting Supershell backdoors and various pen testing tools of Chinese origin. The actor's activities are linked to the exploitation of a specific vulnerability, with a focus on using Chinese cloud providers. Analysis of the infrastructure has revealed TTPs associated with Chaya_004, indicating a sophisticated approach to cyber operations. Mitigation recommendations and proactive response measures have been developed in light of these findings.
